commitTitle: feat(config): add the restricted YAML and JSON profile
summary: Built internal/config/profile, stage B of the configuration pipeline. It implements every requirement in WP-33's scope, and the YAML Test Suite is vendored with its ratchet. Parse runs the byte pre-checks (UTF-8, U+FEFF anywhere, YAML printable set, size). CR LF and CR become LF, which moves no position. The text is cut into documents at marker lines and each document goes through the token pass: anchors, aliases and merge keys are RZ-CFG-003 and non-core tags or %TAG are RZ-CFG-004, collected for the whole file. RZ-CFG-001 (a %YAML version other than 1.2, an invalid token, depth over 64, more than 1,000,000 tokens) stops the file. goccy then parses each document. Ruralz types plain scalars by the YAML 1.2 core schema, converting float text to RFC 8259 form without float64 (R-64). Duplicate keys are RZ-CFG-002 with both positions, a non-mapping root is RZ-CFG-005, and positions are 1-based code points. The JSON front end runs on jsonval and builds trees equal to the YAML twins. Encode / EncodeWith / EncodeJSON are the one emitter: the 02 req 45 quoting rule, "$${" escaping, "---" separators, two-space indent. The YAML Test Suite (data-2022-01-17) is vendored with scripts/update-test-suites.sh and runs under the integration tag against test.event and in.json. The 90 expected failures are 32 profile:anchor, 22 profile:tag, 5 profile:directive, 12 profile:complex-key and 19 reviewed:goccy-v1.19.2/<name>. Three goccy v1.19.2 problems found during the work are fixed inside the package and checked against goccy's own parse, without changing any result for valid YAML. Fuzzing ran FuzzLoadYAML for about 40 minutes in total and the other two targets for 2 to 4 minutes each; every crasher found is now a committed seed.
requirements:
Implemented:
- 01 B 7 (pre-checks), 8 (token pass), 9 (depth algorithm, documents parsed one at a time), 10 (goccy parse; a non-scalar key is RZ-CFG-001), 11 (duplicate keys reported with both positions), 12 (core schema typing, tags, int64 range / .inf / .nan as RZ-CFG-005), 13 (documents), 14 (positions).
- 01 C 15 (JSON, on jsonval per R-30).
- 01 req 31 (render escaping).
- R-64 (float text) and R-29 (one emitter, 02 req 45 quoting).
- 02 2.8: 44 (separators, final newline), 45 (quoting), 46 ("$${"), 47 (EncodeJSON: two-space indent, no HTML escaping, final newline).
- 11 B 18 (YAML Test Suite with the expected-failures ratchet).
- 11 req 15 and 17 shapes at profile level: alias bomb rejected before expansion, depth 65, token floods; 1 MiB hostile inputs stay under 256 MiB peak heap.
- 01 req 53 (ctx between documents, Yield hook) and req 55 (purity).
- Fuzz targets FuzzLoadYAML (the spec's FuzzProfileYAML), FuzzProfileJSON, FuzzEncodeRoundTrip.
- Benchmarks BenchmarkParseYAML (MB/s and allocs/resource), BenchmarkParseYAMLWideMapping, BenchmarkParseJSON, BenchmarkEncode.

Not in this package's scope:
- 02 req 48-49 (CLI exit codes and flags: WP-58/WP-74).
- Resource and document limits and their hostile fixtures, and the conformance fixtures under test/conformance (WP-55/WP-79).

contractRequests: Spec 01 req 8 and 9, risk 1 (wording): goccy v1.19.2's scanner.Scanner.Scan is not incremental; one call returns every remaining token. The profile instead cuts the stream into documents at marker lines (YAML 1.2 c-forbidden, the rule goccy also uses), scans each document on its own, and checks MaxDocumentTokens first against an upper bound computed from the bytes (exact for floods of flow indicators, over-counting quoted and multi-word scalars). The exact count is checked after scanning. Please correct 01 req 8 and 9 and risk 1, and record the byte bound under OQ-configuration-model-18.

Spec 01 req 9 (wording): adopt the refined depth rule. A sequence at its key's column ends at the next key at that column, and a key starts at its first tag or scalar token. The literal rule over-counts documents that alternate keys and zero-indented sequences.

Architecture 2.16, a new resolution: 02 req 46 says write "$${" only where substitution runs, while 01 req 31 says every string value. 01 req 28 has substitution unescape "$${" even in forbidden positions, so only the 01 rule makes render idempotent. profile.Encode follows 01 req 31 (keys are never escaped; EncodeOptions.Verbatim turns escaping off for unsubstituted source trees). Please record which rule wins.

Lead: goccy v1.19.2 has two quadratic paths. parser.parseMap recurses once per mapping entry and copies the entries parsed so far at each level; Context.bufferedSrc trims a clipping block scalar's trailing line breaks one at a time. The profile works around both (split.go for mappings from 256 entries, chomp.go for runs of 8 or more blank lines), and both workarounds are checked against goccy over the YAML Test Suite. Please weigh a goccy upgrade or upstream issues; the reviewed:goccy-v1.19.2 entries in expected-failures.txt are tied to that version.

WP-55 (loader) API: profile.Parse(ctx, src, fileID, path, format, Options) returns ([]Document, diag.List, error). The error is only ctx.Err() or ErrFormat. Use FormatOf for case-sensitive extension matching. Documents with errors are left out, a YAML file with any token-pass finding yields no documents, and per-file findings stop at MaxDiagnostics+1 (default 10,000, matching diag.Collector). Options.Yield receives the worker yield hook of 01 req 53.
WP-58 (render) API: use profile.Encode for rendered Bundles and EncodeWith(..., EncodeOptions{Verbatim: true}) for convert. For --output json, pass EncodeJSON a KindList node of the resource roots.

docs/architecture/02-configuration-model.md, OQ-configuration-model-18 (outside WP-33's paths): please record that the token bound computed from the bytes before tokenizing over-counts indicators inside quoted and block scalars. A document can therefore be refused with RZ-CFG-001 "document is too large to tokenize: estimated more than N tokens" while its exact count is under MaxDocumentTokens: about 1 MB of comma-dense quoted text, or about 1.1 MB of embedded JSON in one block scalar. Review finding 5 offered this as the alternative to making the estimator track quotes and block scalars. A tighter estimator cannot tell from bytes alone whether a quote or '|' starts a scalar in goccy's scanner, so it could undercount and weaken the guarantee that tokens are not built before the limit is checked (01 risk 1).
deviations: Depth algorithm (01 req 9): a sequence written at its key's column ends at the next key at that column, so the literal rule cannot count it again at every key (a document of such keys would otherwise exceed 64). A mapping entry's column is its key node's first tag or scalar token, and an explicit '?' entry's ':' joins its frame.

goccy parses wide block mappings in quadratic time. From 256 entries the profile parses entry by entry (split.go), still with goccy for each key and value. The result equals goccy's whole-document parse on every YAML Test Suite stream with every collection forced through the split, and on the edge cases in TestSplitEdgeCases. Where goccy misparses block structure (for example 0:\n-\n1: nests the key in the empty entry), the split follows YAML 1.2 frames, so such input inside a wide mapping can parse differently than in a small one.

A clipping block scalar followed by 8 or more blank lines is scanned with keep chomping (or strip when its content is all blank) and clipped afterwards (chomp.go). The fuzz target and suite variants check this gives values identical to goccy's own clipping.

MaxDocumentTokens is enforced against the byte bound before tokenizing (see the first contract request), so a document whose true count is just under the limit can be refused when the bound over-counts.

Parse returns a third value (error, for ctx cancellation or an unknown format) and takes Options (MaxBytes, MaxDepth, MaxDocumentTokens, MaxDiagnostics, Yield) instead of the spec's Limits. Per-file findings stop after MaxDiagnostics+1.
goccy errors are matched with errors.As on an interface (GetToken, GetMessage) instead of *yaml.SyntaxError, so goccy's reflection-based root package is not linked into binaries.

JSON front end: integers are normalized (-0 becomes 0) and out-of-int64 integers are RZ-CFG-005, as for YAML, so JSON and YAML twins produce equal trees. A top-level null is RZ-CFG-005 (an object is required), not skipped as YAML null documents are. A leading BOM is RZ-CFG-001 with a byte-order-mark message.
EncodeJSON writes a float with neither fraction nor exponent (YAML 1. becomes text 1) as 1.0, so it stays a float; YAML Encode writes 1.
goccy refuses a tag with no content followed by another token (a: !!str then b: 1), although it is valid YAML. The profile keeps goccy's RZ-CFG-001 for it, and the split parse does the same.

The YAML Test Suite runner checks every non-error case against test.event (structure, typed scalar text, style) and against in.json when present, so the 29 cases without in.json are checked too. Reasons use reviewed:goccy-v1.19.2/<name>, pointing at goccy's own failureTestNames list: goccy GitHub issue numbers could not be looked up, because this session has no GitHub search access.

Fuzz memory check: for inputs over 64 KiB, peak heap growth sampled every 1 ms must stay at or below 256 MiB up to 1 MiB of input. Smaller inputs check total allocation at or below 32 MiB plus 1 KiB per byte, which catches expansion and quadratic parsing. The 2 s per input check was done with a temporary timer during fuzzing; no input exceeded it.
Parse-stage diagnostics carry file, line, column and message but no Resource and no Path, because list types (keyed, set or atomic) are unknown at parse time.

Finding 1: the suggested SequenceEntryType check alone does not make G5U8 (`- [-, -]`) or YJV2 (`[-]`) pass. goccy scans a '-' followed by a flow indicator as a plain string "-", not as a sequence entry. I added a second token-pass check, tokenPass.loneDash: in flow context, a plain scalar "-" that a ':' does not follow at once is RZ-CFG-001, which matches YAML 1.2's ns-plain-first rule. `[-: x]` and `{-: x}` stay valid. With it, both cases pass and are removed from expected-failures.txt.

Finding 5: I took the rewording option, not quote and block-scalar tracking in estimateTokens, for the undercount risk given in contractRequests. The OQ-configuration-model-18 entry is in docs/, outside WP-33's paths, so it is filed as a contract request. Only the internal/config/profile/doc.go package comment was updated to describe the estimate.

Finding 6: I took the 'always split' option over reporting RZ-CFG-001, so `a:\n-\nb: 1` now gives the YAML 1.2 tree {a:[null], b:1} at every width. The test-only setting that turns splitting off (Options.splitAt < 0) still yields goccy's tree; TestSplitParseMatchesGoccy uses it as its reference.

Beyond the findings: the now-real differential found a second keep-chomping bug, fixed in cutBlankRuns. A whitespace-only line can be block-scalar content: with an explicit indentation indicator, goccy adds the spaces past the indentation to the value. The old cut dropped such lines, so the first scan saw an empty scalar and strip chomping removed the content. Each cut run now keeps its first two lines, its longest line and its last line; goccy checks the last line's indentation against the content that follows. Lines holding a tab no longer count as blank.

Finding 3: on a single line, goccy reports a token that follows a tag one column early, the same quirk as block scalar headers. So `a: !!str !!str x` is reported at 1:9, not 1:10; the diagnostic keeps goccy's position, as every other token-pass finding does. `a: !!str\n!!str b: 1` is valid YAML 1.2 (a tagged empty value, then a tagged key) but is now refused by the token pass as "a node has at most one tag". goccy already refused it as "value does not match tag", so what is accepted does not change.

peakHeap (helpers_test.go) now measures live heap objects plus goroutine stacks. This makes every TestHostileInputsBounded case and the FuzzLoadYAML check for inputs over 64 KiB stricter, and all of them still pass. The FuzzLoadYAML check that the byte bound is never below goccy's count now scans the rewritten text, as the loader does. On the raw text, the 60 KB tagged-scalar seed took 13 s in goccy's own clipping.

Linearity tests: comparing allocations at one doubling was noisy, because buffers grow by doubling. TestTaggedBlockScalarBlankLinesAreLinear compares an eightfold scale-up instead (a ratio under 24 when about 8 is linear and 64 is quadratic) and keeps an absolute bound of 256 bytes per input byte plus 8 MiB.

Finding 2: I widened the reviewer's implicit-key check slightly. startsImplicitKey also accepts an empty tagged key (tag directly followed by ':' on its line, e.g. `a: !!map
  !!str : 1`), which goccy parses to {a:{"":1}} the same as without the outer tag. It also skips an anchor and its name after the tag, so `a: !!map
  !!str &x k: v` reports RZ-CFG-003 at the anchor instead of a wrong RZ-CFG-001. The exception applies only in block context: in flow context a tag that follows a tag always belongs to the same node, so `a: [!!str
  !!str x: y]` stays RZ-CFG-001. A chain is still bounded at two tags.

Not fixed (outside both findings): goccy cannot parse a tagged empty value followed by a sibling key (`a: !!str\nb: 1` gives RZ-CFG-001 'unexpected scalar value'). The same goccy error occurs with or without a second tag, and the tag fix does not cause it.

The fixes did not cause this: it was there before them and I found it during this re-review.
remaining.issue:
goccy nests a block-mapping key written at the same column under the empty, `!!map`-tagged value before it. `a: !!map
b: 1` parses with no findings to {a:{b:1}}. In YAML 1.2, b is a sibling of a, and a is an empty node tagged !!map. The same happens for `a: !!map # c
b: 1`, `? a
: !!map
b: 1`, `- !!map
a: 1` and `a:
  - !!map
  b: 1`. The depth algorithm counts by column, so it sees one level while goccy recurses once per line. Measured (overlay test): 255 lines of `kN: !!map` per column, just under splitAt 256, across 63 columns makes a 712 KB input. It parses with no findings to a tree of depth 16,066 against MaxDepth 64, in 6.0 s with 1,679 MiB peak heap. The cost is goccy parser.(*context).withChild, which concatenates path strings, so it grows with depth squared. On one column, 255 lines are accepted at depth 256, but 256 lines take the split parse and fail with "unexpected scalar value". So the result also depends on the mapping's width. Finding 2's fix now admits the tagged-key form too (`!!str k0: !!map
!!str k1: !!map ...`), which behaves the same way. TestHostileInputsBounded and FuzzLoadYAML do not cover this shape.
